What is a forex grey label?

Can I offer both MT4 and MT5?

Yes. Many brokers run both so traders can choose the platform they prefer.

Can I get my own MT4 licence?

Do I need a licence to run a brokerage?

It depends on your business model and where clients are located. Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction.

How long does it take to launch?

Platform setup is usually quicker than the business side. Company formation, payment provider approval and licensing tend to decide the timeline.

Can I move to white label later?

What Is an MT4 Grey Label?

Picture a shopping centre. The owner holds the lease on the whole building, maintains it and keeps the lights on. Individual shops rent space inside, put their own name over the door and run their business however they choose.

An MT4 grey label works in much the same way. A company that holds an MT4 licence runs the server. Your brokerage gets its own space on that server, with your brand facing your clients and a manager account that lets you run your side of things. You decide who your traders are, which groups they sit in, what leverage they get and how your spreads are set.

This matters more for MT4 than for almost any other platform. The vendor no longer issues new MT4 licences. If you want to offer MetaTrader 4 grey label access today, working through an existing licence holder is the realistic way in.

02 / 12

Who Needs an MT4 Grey Label?

This suits brokers whose audience is already comfortable on MT4:

  • Founders targeting traders who have used MT4 for years and don't want to switch
  • IBs who want their clients on a brand they own instead of someone else's
  • Brokers serving expert advisor users, since MT4 EAs don't run on MT5
  • Businesses testing a new region before committing to larger infrastructure
  • Brokers already on MT5 who keep losing prospects that only want MT4

If your plans depend from day one on running the server yourself, a grey label won't give you that, and we'll say so.

03 / 12

Key Features

What's included is confirmed in writing for your package. Most MT4 grey label setups give you:

  • Your brokerage name on the client side of MT4
  • Manager access to open, edit and organise client accounts
  • Leverage and spread control within your groups
  • Separate groups for different account types or client segments
  • Balance adjustments, deposits, withdrawals and credits on trading accounts
  • Margin and equity monitoring across your clients
  • Trading activity and account reports
  • Desktop, web and mobile terminals for your traders
  • A connection point for your CRM through the manager API
  • Support during setup and after you go live
04 / 12

How It Works

Three layers sit on top of each other.

The licence holder runs the bottom layer: the MT4 server itself, its maintenance, updates and the licence that keeps it legitimate.

You run the middle layer through your manager account. That's where your clients live, along with their groups, trading conditions and account balances. Your section is kept separate from any other broker on the same server.

The top layer is everything your traders touch. Your website, your client portal, your onboarding emails and the MT4 terminal they log in to. When someone registers and gets approved in your CRM, the CRM reaches through the manager API and opens their MT4 account. When they deposit, the balance updates. When they trade, the order follows your execution setup.

Knowing which layer owns what makes it far easier to solve problems quickly.

05 / 12

Integrations

An MT4 grey label is the trading engine. These are the parts that turn it into a brokerage:

  • Forex broker CRM for registration, verification, account creation and back office, linked through the manager API
  • PAMM and MAM plugins so money managers can trade on behalf of investors
  • Liquidity and bridge connections, where the grey label arrangement allows
  • Broker website with registration, login and MT4 download pages
  • Payment providers connected through the CRM for deposits and withdrawals
  • Hosting for your website, CRM and other client-facing systems

Every connection is tested end to end before your first real client signs up. Our forex broker CRM page explains the back office in more depth.

06 / 12

With new licences off the table, a grey label is how new brokers offer MT4 today.

Lower Costs at the Start

No licence fees, server hardware or platform engineers to pay for. Your budget can go into marketing, compliance and winning clients.

Traders Feel at Home

Many traders have years of habit on MT4. They know where everything is, which means fewer support questions and quicker first trades.

Control Over What Matters

Your clients, groups, leverage and spreads are yours to manage within the arrangement.

A Base to Build On

Add MT5, plugins or a white label later. Starting on grey label keeps those doors open.

Use Cases

A trading coach has a community of several hundred MT4 users, many running their own EAs. Launching an MT4 grey label lets them trade with the coach's brokerage without rebuilding any of their tools.

An IB has spent years earning rebates on clients who trade under another broker's name. Moving them to an MT4 grey label means setting their own conditions and owning the client relationship.

A broker running MT5 notices a steady stream of prospects asking only for MT4. Adding an MT4 grey label wins those traders without disturbing the existing setup.

A founder wants to test demand in one country before investing heavily. A grey label keeps the first year's costs low while the business proves itself.

10 / 12

Security, Reliability and Support

The licence holder looks after server maintenance, monitoring and updates. On your side, security depends largely on how manager access is handled. Give each person only the permissions their job needs. Someone answering client emails doesn't need the ability to change leverage or apply credits.

Two-step verification on CRM logins, regular access reviews and removing accounts promptly when people leave are simple steps that prevent a lot of trouble.

After launch, we're available for configuration changes, technical issues and new integrations as your brokerage grows.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does an MT4 grey label provider actually do?+

A provider arranges your access on a licensed MT4 server, sets up your manager account and branding, and connects the platform to your CRM and other systems.

Yes, through companies that hold existing MT4 licences. Terms depend on the licence holder, and we confirm them before you commit.

What Is an MT5 Grey Label?

Running a brokerage on MT5 normally means one of two things. Either you hold a licence and operate your own server, which is costly and slow to arrange, or you work with a company that already has that licence and operates the server for you.

The second option is a grey label. The licence holder runs the MT5 server. Your brokerage is given its own section of it, with your brand on the client side and a manager account you use to look after your traders. Groups, leverage, spreads, account balances and reports all sit under your control.

Your traders never deal with the arrangement behind the scenes. They download MT5, find your brokerage, log in and trade.

02 / 13

Why MT5 Rather Than MT4?

MT5 was built as a separate platform, not an update to MT4, and the differences show up in daily trading.

It handles a broader range of markets, including exchange-traded instruments as well as forex and CFDs, so it suits brokers planning a wider product list. Charts come with 21 timeframes instead of 9. Traders get six pending order types, including stop limit orders. Accounts can run in hedging or netting mode. There's a built-in economic calendar, depth of market and a faster strategy tester.

One thing to weigh up: MT5 expert advisors are written in MQL5, and MT4 tools don't carry across automatically. If a large part of your audience relies on MT4 EAs, running both platforms is often the answer.

03 / 13

Who Needs an MT5 Grey Label?

  • New brokers who want to start on the platform with an active development future
  • Brokers planning to add indices, commodities, stocks or futures as they grow
  • Brokers with active technical traders who value extra timeframes and order types
  • MT4 brokers adding a second platform for clients requesting MT5
  • Prop operators who want modern testing tools and multi-account management
04 / 13

  • Branded MT5 access on desktop, web and mobile
  • Manager account for opening, editing and grouping client accounts
  • Leverage, spread and commission settings per group
  • Hedging or netting configuration, depending on the arrangement
  • Equity, margin and exposure monitoring
  • Deposits, withdrawals and credits reflected on trading accounts
  • Trading and account reports
  • Manager API access for CRM and plugin connections
  • Technical support from setup through to life after launch
05 / 13

How It Works

Think of it as a relay.

The licence holder keeps the MT5 server running, handles updates and carries the obligations tied to the licence. That's the first leg.

Your manager account takes the baton. From there, your team configures groups and symbols, sets trading conditions and watches client activity. Your section of the server is kept apart from other brokers using it.

Your systems run the final leg. A trader registers on your website, gets approved in your CRM and has an MT5 account opened automatically through the manager API. Deposits arrive through your payment providers and update their balance. Orders route through your execution setup, whether that's an arrangement through the licence holder or your own liquidity connection.

When each leg knows its job, handoffs stay smooth.

What Is a Forex Liquidity Bridge?

MetaTrader is excellent at showing prices and taking orders. On its own, though, it doesn't connect to the wider market. Something has to sit between your platform and the banks, prime brokers or aggregators supplying prices and filling trades.

That something is a forex liquidity bridge. It works a bit like air traffic control. Prices fly in from your providers, the bridge organises them and passes them to MT4 or MT5. Orders fly out from your traders, and the bridge directs each one to the right destination based on rules you've set, then confirms the result back to the platform.

When it's working well, nobody notices it. When it isn't, traders notice straight away through slow fills, rejected orders or prices that freeze.

To be clear about our part: we set up and configure bridge technology and help you connect to liquidity providers. We aren't a liquidity provider ourselves, and pricing and terms are agreed directly between you and each provider.

Whether you can use your own bridge also depends on your platform arrangement. Some grey label setups include execution through the licence holder, while others allow your own connections. We'll explain what yours supports.

  • Detailed logs for every order and fill

04 / 12

How It Works

Prices In

Your providers stream prices to the bridge. If there's more than one, the bridge combines them into a single feed, applies any markup you've chosen and sends the result to MT4 or MT5.

Orders Out

A trader clicks buy or sell. The platform hands the order to the bridge, which checks your rules. Depending on the client group, instrument or size, the order might go straight to the best available provider, be kept internal or be split.

Confirmation Back

The fill returns through the bridge to the platform, and the trader sees their position. The whole round trip usually takes a fraction of a second.

You set the rules. The bridge applies them consistently, trade after trade.

05 / 12

Integrations

  • Liquidity providers, prime brokers and aggregators you contract with

06 / 12

Your Execution Model, Your Way

Send everything to the market, keep it internal, or set rules for a mix. You can treat different clients differently as your book develops.

Less Reliance on One Source

Multiple providers give you more pricing options and a fallback if one has trouble.

Both Platforms Covered

MT4 and MT5 can be connected to the same liquidity setup, keeping operations consistent.

A Record of Every Trade

Execution logs help you investigate disputes and review performance.

Ready for Growth

Adding providers, instruments and rules is far easier when the bridge is set up properly from the start.

07 / 12

Implementation

We talk through your risk approach, instruments, expected volume, platforms and any providers you're considering.

Check What Your Platform Allows

We confirm whether your MT4 or MT5 arrangement supports your own bridge connection.

Choose the Setup

We recommend a bridge approach and help you evaluate liquidity options. Agreements are made directly between you and each provider.

Configure

Connections, symbol mapping, routing rules, markups and failover are set up.

Test

Test orders run across instruments, sizes and conditions to check pricing, fills and rejections.

Go Live and Adjust

After launch, we help refine rules as you learn how your clients trade.

08 / 12

Main revenueSpreads, markups, commissionIncludes client trading outcomesCombination
Bridge roleCentralSmallerCentral
SuitsBrokers minimising exposureBrokers with strong risk managementMost growing brokers

Each model has its own risks, and regulators in some jurisdictions take a view on how brokers manage client flow. Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction, so factor your licensing position into the choice.

09 / 12

Use Cases

A new broker on MT4 wants every trade passed to the market while volumes are low. A single provider connection with simple routing does the job.

A broker running MT4 and MT5 wants both platforms using the same providers and rules. One bridge setup covers them.

A broker identifies a group of consistently profitable clients. Routing rules send those accounts to the market, while other flow is handled internally.

A broker loses an afternoon of trading during a provider outage. Adding a second provider with failover reduces the chance of it happening again.

10 / 12

Reliability and Support

Execution issues tend to appear when markets move fastest, around major news or session opens. Monitoring and failover are as important as the original setup.

Access to routing and markup settings should be limited to your dealing and risk staff, with changes logged.

After launch, we help with new instruments, extra providers, rule changes and troubleshooting. Fill quality and liquidity availability depend on market conditions and your providers, so they can't be guaranteed, but we'll help make sure your setup does its part well.

No. We configure bridge technology and help you connect to liquidity providers. Terms come from your own agreements with them.

Can one bridge connect MT4 and MT5?+

In many setups, yes, depending on the bridge software and your platform arrangements.

It depends on the arrangement. Some include execution through the licence holder, while others allow your own connection.

How many liquidity providers can I connect?+

That depends on the bridge software. Multiple providers allow price aggregation and failover.

Can I apply my own markups?+

Yes. Markups can usually be set by instrument or client group.

It gives you control and options. Actual execution quality also depends on your providers, market conditions and configuration.

MANAGED ACCOUNTS

PAMM and MAM Plugin for MT4 and MT5 Brokers

Talented traders attract followers who'd like them to trade on their behalf. A PAMM MAM plugin lets that happen on your MT4 or MT5 platform, with allocations, fees and investor statements calculated for you.

⌁PAMM & MAM PluginsConnected brokerage systems
a PAMM MAM Plugin?
PAMM and MAM, Explained Simply
It?

On this page

What Is a PAMM MAM Plugin?PAMM and MAM, Explained SimplyWho Needs It?Key FeaturesHow It WorksIntegrationsBenefitsImplementationUse CasesRegulationSecurity and SupportFrequently Asked Questions

01 / 13

What Is a PAMM MAM Plugin?

Say a trader on your platform has a strong track record, and twenty people want to put money behind their strategy. Without the right tools, the options are messy. Investors could share logins, which is risky. The trader could place the same trade twenty times, which is impractical. Or someone could split results by hand at the end of each month, which invites errors.

A PAMM MAM plugin solves this properly. It sits on top of MT4 or MT5 and lets one manager handle many investors at once. The plugin works out who owns what, applies each trade fairly, charges fees under agreed rules and reports results back to everyone.

02 / 13

PAMM and MAM, Explained Simply

PAMM: A Shared Pot

With PAMM, investors' money goes into one shared pot. The manager trades the pot as a whole. When the pot gains or loses, each investor's slice moves by the same percentage, because their share was set by how much they contributed.

It's easy for investors to follow and requires nothing from them except choosing a manager. It's a common choice for MT4 PAMM and MT5 PAMM offerings aimed at passive investors.

MAM: One Conductor, Many Instruments

With MAM, every investor keeps a separate trading account. The manager places a trade once, and the plugin copies it across all connected accounts using a chosen allocation method, such as account equity, balance, fixed lots or a set percentage.

Because accounts stay distinct, the manager can treat them a little differently where needed. A MAM plugin for MT4 or MT5 suits managers looking after clients with different account sizes or preferences.

Which One Fits?

PAMMMAM
Investor fundsCombined into one poolHeld in separate accounts
How trades applyShared by percentage of the poolCopied by allocation method
Control per investorLimitedGreater
Simplicity for investorsVery simpleSimple, with more options

Passive investors following one strategy

03 / 13

Who Needs It?

  • Brokers wanting to attract skilled traders who bring their own investors
  • Money managers looking for a professional way to trade for multiple clients
  • Copy-trading businesses offering strategies to followers
  • Prop operators managing many accounts from one place
  • Signal providers ready to manage accounts rather than send alerts
04 / 13

Key Features

Exact features depend on the plugin and platform arrangement, confirmed before setup. Typically:

  • PAMM, MAM or both, on MT4 and MT5
  • Multi-account terminal for trading many accounts from one screen
  • Allocation methods including equity, balance, lots and percentage
  • Performance fees, management fees and other fee structures
  • High-water mark logic so performance fees apply only to new gains
  • Investor joining and leaving through the client portal
  • Investor deposits and withdrawals with your approval process
  • Dashboards for managers and investors
  • Investor statements and performance reports
  • Connection through the manager API to your CRM
05 / 13

How It Works

The plugin runs alongside your MT4 or MT5 server and communicates through the manager API.

A manager is set up with a master account and their offering, whether PAMM or MAM, along with fee terms. Investors find the offering in your client portal, join and fund their participation through the CRM.

When the manager trades, the plugin applies the results to each investor according to the model. Fees are calculated at the agreed intervals. Investors see their balance, returns and fees in their dashboard. When someone wants to withdraw, the request goes through your usual CRM approval flow.

Your brokerage stays in control throughout, with full records of every allocation and fee.

06 / 13

Integrations

  • MT4 and MT5 through the manager API, including our MT4 grey label and MT5 grey label setups
  • Forex broker CRM for investor onboarding, deposits, withdrawals and reporting
  • Client portal where investors browse, join and monitor managed accounts
  • Payment providers for investor funding
  • Email notifications for statements and account changes
07 / 13

Benefits

New Reasons for Traders to Choose You

Experienced managers look for brokers with proper fund-management tools. Offering them can bring both managers and their investors to your platform.

Accurate, Automatic Allocation

No manual splitting of results and no spreadsheets at month end.

Fees Handled Fairly

Performance and management fees are calculated consistently under agreed rules, including high-water marks.

Investors Can See What's Happening

Clear statements build confidence and reduce questions.

Easier Oversight

Every allocation, fee and transaction is recorded for your brokerage to review.

08 / 13

Implementation

Shape Your Offering

We discuss PAMM, MAM or both, your managers, fee models and which platforms they'll use.

Configure the Plugin

Allocation methods, fee rules, groups and terminal access are set up.

Connect to Your CRM

Investor flows are added to the client portal and linked through the manager API.

Test Every Scenario

Test managers and investors run through deposits, trades, fees, top-ups and withdrawals.

Launch

Your first managers go live, with support as your offering grows.

09 / 13

Use Cases

A trader with a respected public record wants to accept investors. A PAMM account lets people join with any amount and share results proportionally.

A money manager looks after clients with very different balances. MAM keeps each account separate while every trade is copied with the right allocation.

A broker wants to stand out to professional traders. Adding forex PAMM software and a multi-account terminal gives them the tools they look for.

A prop operator runs many accounts and needs to trade them together. The multi-account terminal makes it manageable.

10 / 13

Regulation

When someone trades money that belongs to other people, regulators often take an interest. Rules for managed-account products differ widely, and may apply to the broker, the manager or both.

Regulatory requirements for managed-account products vary by jurisdiction. Get legal advice for your markets before launching a PAMM or MAM offering. We supply the technology, not regulatory permission.

11 / 13

Security and Support

Allocation rules and fee settings directly affect investors' money, so access to change them should be limited and logged. Managers should only see their own investors, and investors only their own accounts.

After launch, we help with new managers, rule changes, technical issues and integration updates.

12 / 13

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the plugin work on both MT4 and MT5?+

PAMM and MAM tools are available for both platforms, depending on the plugin and your arrangement.

What's the main difference between PAMM and MAM?+

PAMM pools funds and shares results by percentage. MAM keeps separate accounts and copies trades across them.

Can managers charge performance fees?+

Yes. Performance fees, management fees and high-water marks can usually be configured.

How do investors join a manager?+

Through your client portal, with funding handled by your CRM and payment providers.

Can investors withdraw at any time?+

Withdrawal terms are set by you and the manager, and processed through your CRM approval flow.

Do I need a licence to offer managed accounts?+

It depends on your jurisdiction and where your clients are. Regulatory requirements for managed-account products vary.

pages.content:
LAUNCH GUIDE

How to Start a Forex Brokerage with an MT4 or MT5 Grey Label

Most people who want to start a forex brokerage already understand trading. What they're less sure about is the machinery behind it. This guide explains the technology a brokerage runs on, the order to put it together and the choices that matter most along the way.

Explore the details ↓Discuss your setup ↗

The Short Version
Why a Grey Label Is the Usual Sta
The Technology Stack, Piece by Pi

On this page

01 / 11

The Short Version

To start a forex brokerage on a grey label, you'll need six things working together: a legal entity, a trading platform, a CRM, a way to execute trades, a way to take payments and a website. Get those in place, connect them properly, test the whole journey and you have a brokerage ready to open its doors.

The rest of this page explains each piece and how they fit.

02 / 11

Why a Grey Label Is the Usual Starting Point

There are three broad ways to put MetaTrader in front of clients.

You could hold a platform licence yourself and run your own server. That's expensive, slow to arrange and, for MT4, no longer possible for new applicants. You could take a white label, which gives deeper branding and control but costs considerably more and has become harder to secure. Or you could start on a grey label, operating your brand on a licence holder's server with manager access to your own clients and trading conditions.

For a first brokerage, grey label tends to win on cost, speed and practicality. It lets you prove the business before committing to heavier infrastructure. Our MT4 grey label and MT5 grey label pages explain each in detail.

03 / 11

The Technology Stack, Piece by Piece

Trading Platform

This is where your clients analyse markets and place trades. On a grey label, you'll offer MT4, MT5 or both. You control client groups, leverage, spreads and account settings through your manager account.

CRM and Client Portal

The CRM is your back office. It captures registrations, runs identity checks, opens trading accounts through the manager API, records deposits and withdrawals, manages IB partners and produces reports. The client portal, or trader's room, is the part your traders use to verify, fund and manage their accounts.

Liquidity and Bridge

If client trades are going to the market, a bridge connects your platform to liquidity providers and applies your routing rules. Some grey label arrangements include execution through the licence holder, while others allow your own bridge.

Payments

Payment service providers process deposits and withdrawals. Integrated with your CRM, they credit trading accounts automatically.

Website

Your website introduces your brokerage, explains accounts and conditions, carries legal pages and sends new traders into registration.

Hosting

Your CRM, website and any extra tools need reliable hosting with monitoring and backups. On a grey label, the trading server itself is run by the licence holder.

Optional Extras

PAMM and MAM plugins for money managers, extra languages, prop firm tools and more can be added at launch or later.

04 / 11

MT4 or MT5: Making the Platform Choice

This decision deserves a little time, because it shapes your audience.

MT4 remains popular with traders who've used it for years, especially those running expert advisors written in MQL4. If your target clients are experienced forex traders with established tools, MT4 matters.

MT5 covers a wider range of markets, including exchange-traded instruments, and offers more timeframes, more order types and both hedging and netting accounts. It's where the platform vendor focuses new development. If you plan to expand beyond forex or attract newer traders, MT5 makes sense.

Both is a common answer. Running MT4 and MT5 side by side lets traders choose, and your CRM can manage accounts on both.

Whichever you choose, confirm grey label availability and terms in writing before building around it.

05 / 11

The Launch Stages

Groundwork

Define who your clients are, where they live, what they'll trade and how you'll earn. Decide whether trades will be passed to the market, handled internally or a mix. These answers drive everything that follows.

Company and Regulatory Position

Set up a legal entity to contract with your technology and payment partners. Work out, with legal advice, whether your business model and target markets require a licence. Registering a company isn't the same as being licensed, and regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction.

Platform Setup

Agree your grey label terms, then configure groups, symbols, leverage, spreads and branding on your manager account.

CRM Configuration

Set up account types, KYC steps, approval rules, staff roles and IB structure, then connect the CRM to MT4 or MT5.

Liquidity

Connect your bridge and providers, or confirm how execution works through your grey label arrangement. Set routing rules that match your risk approach.

Payments

Apply to payment providers early, since approval often takes longer than the technology. Once approved, they're integrated with the CRM. Approval is always the provider's decision.

Website

Build a site that connects registration and login to the CRM and offers platform downloads. Make sure legal and risk pages reflect your actual position.

Testing

Run test clients through registration, verification, deposit, trading and withdrawal. Check IB tracking, emails and every payment method.

Launch and Support

Go live, start marketing and lean on support while your team gets used to the systems.

06 / 11

How the Pieces Talk to Each Other

Here's the client journey once everything is connected.

A trader lands on your website and registers. The CRM records them as a lead. They upload documents in the trader's room, and compliance approves them. The CRM opens their MT4 or MT5 account through the manager API and emails their login.

They deposit through an integrated payment provider. The CRM credits their trading balance. They download the platform from your site and trade. Orders route through your bridge or the grey label execution arrangement. Later, they request a withdrawal, finance approves it, and the balance updates.

When any link is missing, someone on your team fills the gap manually. When everything's connected, the journey runs largely on its own.

07 / 11

Mistakes First-Time Founders Make

  • Picking a jurisdiction before knowing where clients will come from
  • Building around a platform before confirming grey label terms
  • Launching without a CRM and handling accounts by hand
  • Waiting until the end to apply to payment providers
  • Choosing a website that isn't connected to the CRM
  • Ignoring liquidity until clients start complaining about fills
  • Underestimating the support needed in the first few months
08 / 11

What Support Looks Like After Launch

The first weeks after launch are when real clients find the gaps that testing missed. Questions come up about manager settings, CRM workflows, payment flows and platform access.

Having a technology partner who knows your setup makes a big difference here. We stay involved for configuration changes, troubleshooting and adding new pieces as you grow, from MT5 to PAMM tools to new payment methods.

09 / 11

Where We Fit

We set up and connect the technology side: your MT4 or MT5 grey label, CRM, liquidity connections, website and hosting, plus plugins where needed. Everything is tested together before launch.

We're a technology provider, not a broker, regulator or payment provider. Licensing decisions, provider approvals and running the brokerage day to day remain with you and the relevant authorities. We'll be clear about that from the first conversation.

10 / 11

Frequently Asked Questions

What do I need to start a forex brokerage?+

A legal entity, a trading platform, a CRM, an execution setup, payment providers and a website, all connected. Depending on your model and markets, you may also need a licence.

Should I choose MT4 or MT5?+

MT4 suits traders attached to its interface and MQL4 tools. MT5 suits brokers expanding beyond forex or attracting newer traders. Many brokers offer both.

Do I need my own liquidity provider?+

It depends on your grey label arrangement and execution model. Some arrangements include execution, while others let you connect your own providers.

Can I start without a CRM?+

Technically, yes, but it quickly becomes unmanageable. A CRM automates onboarding, account creation and payments.

How long does it take to launch?+

The technology can often be ready sooner than the business side. Company setup, licensing and payment provider approval usually set the timeline.

Do I need a licence?+

It depends on your business model and where your clients are. Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction, so take legal advice.

Can I upgrade later?+

Yes. You can add MT5, plugins or more providers, and move to white label if one becomes available and makes sense.

11 / 11

Tell us about the brokerage you want to build and the traders you want to serve. We'll lay out the stack, the stages and the platform choice that fits, so you can start your forex brokerage on solid ground.

Technology Solutions to Scale Your Forex Brokerage

Growth exposes every weak spot in a brokerage's technology. We help established brokers strengthen the CRM, add products like PAMM and MAM, automate the busywork, improve liquidity and build infrastructure that keeps pace with more clients.

01 / 10

When Growth Starts to Hurt

The first year of a brokerage is usually about getting clients. The next stage is about handling them.

At a few hundred traders, small inefficiencies don't matter much. Someone credits a deposit by hand. Someone emails an IB their commission figures. Someone restarts a slow server on a Friday night. At a few thousand traders, those same inefficiencies become the reason support queues grow, finance falls behind and good clients drift away.

Scaling a forex brokerage isn't just about adding clients. It's about making sure each extra client costs you less effort than the one before.

02 / 10

Who This Is For

  • Brokers whose operations team spends more time on admin than on clients
  • Brokerages with a CRM that's struggling under current volumes
  • Brokers wanting new products to attract larger or more experienced traders
  • Firms whose execution setup is showing strain as volumes rise
  • Brokers entering new markets that need new payments, languages and tools
  • Brokerages whose hosting slows down during busy periods
03 / 10

Where to Focus

CRM: The Engine Room

A CRM that worked at launch may now be the main thing holding you back. Common signs include slow pages, missing automation, an awkward client portal, weak reporting and an IB area partners don't trust.

Upgrading might mean reconfiguring what you have, adding modules or migrating to a more capable system. Client records, documents, account links and history move across with checks. Our forex broker CRM page explains what a modern setup should handle.

PAMM and MAM: Products That Bring Bigger Accounts

Experienced money managers often bring investors with them. Offering PAMM and MAM tools gives those managers a reason to choose your brokerage, and gives you a product competitors may not have.

The plugin connects to MT4 or MT5 and your CRM, so investors join and fund through the client portal and receive clear statements. Regulatory requirements for managed-account products vary by jurisdiction, so take legal advice before launching. Our PAMM / MAM plugin page covers the details.

Automation: Taking Out the Repetitive Work

Look at what your team does over and over. Opening accounts. Crediting deposits. Chasing missing documents. Sending login details. Calculating partner payouts. Producing weekly reports.

Most of these can run automatically through the CRM and its connections to the platform and payment providers. Staff time then goes to exceptions, client relationships and decisions that need a person.

Liquidity: Execution That Holds Up Under Load

More volume puts more pressure on execution. If you rely on a single provider, an outage hurts more. If routing rules haven't changed since launch, they may no longer fit your book.

Improvements can include adding providers, setting up failover, refining routing for different client groups and improving execution monitoring, where your platform arrangement allows. Our liquidity and bridge page explains the options.

Integrations: Connecting the Tools You've Added

Growing brokers tend to collect tools: a live chat here, a marketing platform there, a new payment provider, an identity verification service. When these aren't connected, information gets stuck in separate places.

Linking them to the CRM means every team sees the full picture, and clients don't have to repeat themselves.

Infrastructure: Room to Breathe

As traffic and client numbers rise, hosting that once felt fine can start to slow. Better capacity, monitoring, backups and server locations closer to your clients help keep the portal and website responsive when it matters. Our hosting page explains what's covered.

Client Growth: Supporting New Markets

Expanding into new regions usually brings new payment preferences, languages and expectations. Adding local payment providers, after their approval, and language versions of your website and portal helps new clients feel at home. Check how expansion affects your regulatory position before marketing to new countries.

04 / 10

How We Approach Scaling

Assess

We review your platform setup, CRM, plugins, liquidity, payments, website and hosting, and talk to your team about where time is being lost.

Prioritise

We identify which improvements will have the biggest effect and agree a sensible order. Not everything needs to change at once.

Scope in Writing

Each change is defined clearly, including what moves, what stays and how clients will be affected.

Build and Migrate in Stages

Upgrades are rolled out step by step, with data migrations checked and timing chosen to avoid busy trading periods where possible.

Test in Parallel

New systems are tested alongside existing ones before clients are switched over.

Support Through the Change

We stay involved as your team adapts, and afterwards as new needs come up.

06 / 10

Benefits of Scaling the Right Way

Lower Cost Per Client

Automation means each new trader adds less workload than before.

A Better Experience for Traders

Faster onboarding, quicker deposits and a responsive portal help you keep the clients you win.

New Revenue Streams

Products like PAMM and MAM can attract managers, investors and larger accounts.

Steadier Execution

Stronger liquidity setups reduce the impact of provider issues and busy markets.

Confidence to Expand

When your systems are ready, entering new markets becomes a business decision rather than a technical worry.

07 / 10

Use Cases

A broker's finance team spends most of every Monday matching deposits. Automating payment crediting through the CRM frees the team for higher-value work.

A brokerage keeps losing experienced money managers to competitors. Adding a MAM plugin with clear investor reporting brings them in, along with their investors.

A broker running only MT4 with a single liquidity provider adds MT5, a second provider and failover as volumes climb.

A broker expanding into a new region adds local payment methods and a translated portal, and sees funding rates rise.

08 / 10

Security as You Grow

More staff, systems and integrations mean more access points. As you scale, review permissions, tighten admin rights, enable two-step verification everywhere and make sure backups cover every new system. We build these checks into each upgrade.

09 / 10

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know what to upgrade first?+

Start with whatever costs your team the most time or your clients the most frustration. Our assessment helps identify that.

Can my existing CRM be upgraded, or do I need a new one?+

It depends on the system. Sometimes reconfiguration is enough. Other times, a migration to a more capable CRM is the better option.

Will upgrades disrupt my clients?+

Changes are staged and tested in parallel to keep disruption to a minimum.

Can I add PAMM or MAM to my current setup?+

Usually, yes. Plugins connect to MT4 or MT5 and your CRM through the manager API.

Can I add liquidity providers on a grey label?+

It depends on your grey label arrangement. We'll confirm what's possible.
